IPFX Markets on phones

Built overnight, 13 November 2026. Nothing has been published: the website and the app stores are unchanged.

Ready on its own branch: mobile/phone-ui Desktop unchanged, checked element by element Works on iPhone and Android, 320 to 430px wide, and sideways Not yet tried on a real phone with a signed-in account

What it looks like

These screenshots come from a phone-sized browser with a sample account that has 2 open trades. There are four tabs along the bottom: Chart, Trade, Positions and Account. Every button runs the same code as desktop, so stops, risk checks and fills work the same way.

Phone turned sideways

How to get it on your phone

1 · Try it now, without publishing

Over your home Wi-Fi

  1. In the folder ipfx-mobile\mobile, right-click preview-on-my-phone.ps1 and choose Run with PowerShell.
  2. If Windows asks whether Python can use networks, choose Allow for private networks.
  3. Scan the QR code that opens with your phone's camera. The phone must be on the same Wi-Fi.
  4. iPhone: in Safari tap Share, then Add to Home Screen. Android: in Chrome open the menu, then Add to Home screen.

This uses the real IPFX servers, so signing in and placing trades are real. Close the window to stop it.

2 · Android app file

An .apk for your Android phone

  1. Right-click mobile\build-android-app.ps1 and choose Run with PowerShell.
  2. The first time, it downloads Java and Google's Android tools (about 1.5 GB) and shows Google's Android SDK licence for you to accept. I did not accept it for you.
  3. The app is saved to your Desktop as IPFX-Markets.apk. Send it to your phone and open it.

Not built yet, because the build needs you to accept that licence. Java and the Android tools aren't on your PC yet; the script downloads them.

3 · When you want it live

So every trader can install it

  1. Tell me to publish it, or merge mobile/phone-ui into main.
  2. Traders open ipfxcapital.com/trading.html on their phone. Android shows an Install button, and iPhone shows a short "Add to Home Screen" guide.
  3. To make the Android app update with the website automatically, rebuild it with -Mode live.
Later · App Store and Google Play

Store listings

The iPhone and Android projects are ready in mobile/. Listing them needs company developer accounts (Apple costs $99 a year and Google $25 once; both ask a company for a D-U-N-S number). You also need an iPhone build made on a Mac or a cloud Mac, a store review, and a demo login for the reviewers. Apple asks for trading apps to be submitted by the company that provides the service, and anything bought inside the iPhone app must go through Apple's payments.

What changed

  • Markets on phones:
    • a tab bar along the bottom;
    • a Sell/Buy strip under the chart that opens the order ticket;
    • open and closed trades shown as cards;
    • a full-screen instrument search with a Cancel button;
    • trade dialogs that slide up from the bottom;
    • stop and target lines that are easier to drag with a finger;
    • the top-bar extras (Restart, Switch to v2, Tour) moved into the Account tab;
    • a tour that never covers the thing it points at.
  • Sign-in sheet: phone wording, a close button, and Create account and Forgot password links.
  • Install as an app: the Markets app icon and name, an install button on Android, an Add to Home Screen guide on iPhone, and a clear offline page that says open trades keep their stops.
  • Website pages on phones: fields no longer make iPhones zoom in, the menu button sits on the right, the dashboard header and account filters fit the screen, and the login button is bigger.
  • App project for iPhone and Android in mobile/. The Android app only asks for internet access and does not back up the signed-in session.

Checks

  • Desktop Markets was compared with the live version at 1440, 1280, 1024 and 800px: all 2,667 elements are in exactly the same place.
  • New automatic phone tests check:
    • four tabs, with one panel shown at a time;
    • no sideways scrolling at 320, 360, 390 and 430px;
    • buttons at least 44px tall;
    • nothing new showing on desktop;
    • the phone layout never places or closes a trade by itself.
  • Full test suite: 1,483 passed and 1 failed. The failure (hub-account-push) happens the same way on the live version because a test library is missing, so it is not caused by this work.
